These two new peer_* headlines paraphrase it as «другое устройство», so the namespace has 1/3 «пир» and 2/3 «устройство». The meaning is correct and readable; the defect is terminology consistency, not comprehension.

scrutiny.ui.mesh.mesh_reach.addresses_tried: ACCEPTED. «Попытки подключения» names the connection attempts rather than the addresses; the rows underneath print the addresses, and the heading reads naturally as their label. Sibling locales keep the object literal («Direcciones probadas», «Adresses essayées», «已尝试的地址»), so a stricter rendering would be «Проверенные адреса», but it is not recommended here: it is less precise about attempts and no clearer in a narrow panel.
scrutiny.ui.mesh.mesh_reach.handshake_refused_hin: ACCEPTED. «устройство, удалённое из сети» uses the postposed participle with its «из сети» complement, so it unambiguously means a device REMOVED from the network; the prenominal «удалённое устройство» would have been the ambiguous remote reading. «эпоха совпадает» and «приводят к отказу в рукопожатии» preserve the check-not-cause framing and the two named causes.
scrutiny.ui.mesh.mesh_reach.attempt_bad_address: ACCEPTED. «некорректный адрес» is the standard professional rendering of bad address; the literal «плохой адрес» would be unidiomatic.
